thread:
maria: Quick proposal — add a lightweight SDK middleware that performs an in-flight route negotiation with the control plane. Goal: allow client to indicate preferred routing policy (latency/cost/region) and receive a compact route decision with fallback hints. This will affect headers, telemetry fields, and quota attribution. Anyone opposed?

chris: Sounds useful. How would it differ from current routehint header?

lucas: Main diff is two-way: client proposes preference, server responds with chosen route id + reason + a short fallback chain. We can avoid heavy payloads. Concern: telemetry headers could balloon.

raj: Backcompat question — if older SDKs call the API, should server assume default policy? We can't break existing route semantics.

maria: Yes, absolutely must be opt-in. Plan is: middleware only sends X-RW-Route-Handshake when the SDK runtime flag is enabled. Server treats absence as "no-handshake" and follows existing logic.

teresa: For rollout UX: we should gate on tenant feature-flag, client runtime opt-in, and console toggle that shows "handshake-enabled" tenants. Devex needs a short migration guide.

andy: Telemetry wise, we should limit new metrics to a few counters: route_handshake_sent, handshake_success, handshake_fallback. Avoid adding per-request verbose tags by default. Sampling can increase detail for a small subset.

andy: Also propose we add aggregated console tiles: policy_source, route_decisions_count, fallback_rate.

lucas: Agreed. Also we must ensure quota accounting doesn't double-count tokens when fallback triggers secondary model. We need an idempotency/attribution marker.

raj: Suggest header X-RW-Route-Session which is a short uuid for the request group. Use it so billing/quotas attribute to the originating session, not the fallback.

maria: Nice. Example header plan:

```
X-RW-Route-Handshake: v1;pref=latency
X-RW-Route-Session: 9a8f7c2b
```

teresa: For SDK changes, keep surface minimal: add middleware factory with signature (pref: string, opt?: {sampleRate:number}) => Handler. Default is off. Ship in minor release.

chris: Are we changing any existing header names? That would be breaking.

maria: No renames. New headers only, and server tolerates missing ones. We may publish a compatibility matrix in the release notes.

kev: Test plan: 1) unit tests for header injection; 2) integration test with control plane emulator to ensure fallback chain is respected; 3) quota integration tests to validate single attribution. I'll add e2e.

lucas: Console work: add a small badge on tenant page when handshake opt-in is active. Also expose a timeseries for handshake_success vs fallback. Make sampling configurable to avoid noise.

andy: Telemetry detail: default sampling 1% for full route decision payloads. Counters always emitted.

maria: Implementation owners: SDKs — @teresa (python/ts), @chris (go + core lib). Console/telemetry — @lucas and @andy. Quota/billing — @raj and @kev. I'll open a tracking RFC.

chris: One more: make sure the middleware has a clear upgrade path. If we add v2 handshake later, include version in header so server can negotiate.

maria: Yup: X-RW-Route-Handshake: v1;pref=cost -> future v2 can be v2;pref=...

dev-bot: NOTE: created issue RW-PLAT-4821 for "SDK route handshake: RFC & implementation"

teresa: I'll draft the SDK PR template and migration guide. Can we aim for feature-flag rollout to 10% tenants in two weeks after merge?

maria: Sounds good. Action items: teresa open PR and docs, lucas add console tile mock, andy add metrics plan, kev add e2e tests, raj confirm quota attribution behavior. I'll post RFC link once it's up. :thumbsup:
